LIMIT counts additional attempts and is 0 through 100.
This inline ACTION block is the only source of attempt bounds; total attempts are at most 1 + LIMIT and the first successful attempt ends retrying.
A handler using core.retry authorizes this declared RETRY and its resolved limit must equal this LIMIT.

RETRY.WHEN defaults to TRUE and RETRY.DELAY defaults to DURATION(0, unit.second). A false condition or a refused safety check prevents another attempt without manufacturing count exhaustion or success.
Count exhaustion occurs only after 1 + LIMIT actual unsuccessful attempts.
RETRY.HANDLER is in scope only for diagnostics raised by an attempt of the ACTION declaring this RETRY, including the first attempt.
HANDLER is an invocation site; OPERATION selects and invokes one operation under the ACTION contract.

EVENT names the event this handler activates on; the closed event model in statuses_and_errors_v0.3.0.json#/event_model raises events only from emitted diagnostics and selects at most one handler per raised diagnostic.
A required TARGET may be omitted only under the handler-context binding for REFERENCE[ACTION] or REFERENCE[meta.execution_unit] targets.
LIMIT is exactly the limit named parameter of the selected operation and is legal only when that operation registers it.
FALLBACK admits one REF to a HANDLER, or one operation identifier that requires no named parameter and whose required TARGET the handler-context binding supplies.
An injected handler-context target identifies the active owning invocation aggregate; the failed child attempt remains immutable evidence. Explicit targets follow the selected operation contract.
At most one handler is selected through event attachments; direct acyclic FALLBACK calls may invoke another HANDLER without a second event selection.

execution_graph_contract.candidate_graph: Build the complete finite structural activation graph from EXECUTE. Include both IF branches and each FOR EACH body as source templates for static checking. TASK execution fields, PHASE and SEQUENCE executable children, the selected STEP arm, and a root TEST TASK or ACTION activate execution units. Ordinary REF, TARGET, check references, OUTPUT reads, BEFORE and AFTER never activate a producer. Explicit graph-valued operation invocations create their own child invocation under the same rules.
execution_graph_contract.child_order: TASK execution-bearing PHASE, SEQUENCE, and ACTION fields contribute children in source field order; each reference LIST expands left to right. PHASE and SEQUENCE executable children contribute in lexical order, including STEP, nested SEQUENCE where legal, IF and FOR EACH. A STEP selected reference LIST expands left to right. These are explicit exceptions to otherwise nonsemantic field order.
execution_graph_contract.activation_identity: An execution-unit source declaration has one structural activation path per candidate invocation. Multiple structural paths to the same declaration use error.execution.order before effects, including mutually exclusive branches. Structural cycles use error.reference.cycle. Explicit bounded FOR EACH instances and RETRY attempts replicate their source template with distinct invocation identities and are not duplicate activation.
execution_graph_contract.ordering: TASK and STEP child groups are sequential. PHASE and SEQUENCE use declared MODE, defaulting to mode.sequential. Sequential lexical order contributes required predecessor edges. BEFORE and AFTER add edges and never reverse a sequential edge. Endpoints must be distinct sibling execution units in the same container and iteration context; other endpoints and ordering cycles use error.execution.order. Ordering references never expand reachability. A skipped predecessor satisfies ordering completion but supplies no missing value.
execution_graph_contract.parallel: mode.parallel omits implicit sequential edges but retains BEFORE and AFTER edges. Every included pair must have proven independence: no conflicting writes, read/write dependency, shared mutable binding, or conflicting output destination. Disjoint output paths alone are insufficient. Result collection and diagnostics use declared child order, never finish order. Independent eligible children may execute in any order.
execution_graph_contract.loop_instances: FOR EACH evaluates its finite snapshot once at reachability. Iterations run sequentially in registered LIST or SET order; each body finishes before the next starts. Instance identity includes the full enclosing iteration-index path. The local binding is visible only within its body and resolves to that exact instance.
execution_graph_contract.successor: A declared successor is the unique next reachable sibling in the containing sequential group, ascending finished enclosing sequential containers when necessary. Dynamic applicability is evaluated normally. Continuation invents no unit; an absent successor or ambiguous parallel continuation uses error.execution.order.

project_contract.identity: A project exists only where explicit source declares one. A document whose LCL VERSION is 0.3.0 and whose SPECIFICATION KIND is kind.project is a project entry. No directory, file name, host manifest or tool setting makes a document a project entry, a project part, or a member of a project.
project_contract.entry: An evaluation has exactly one root source unit. When that root is a kind.project entry, the evaluation is a project evaluation of that entry. The entry's file name has no meaning; main.lcl is only a conventional name. A kind.project document that is not the evaluation root, including one named by a PART, IMPORT or EXTENSION, uses error.project.placement at its SPECIFICATION KIND value.
project_contract.parts: The project parts are exactly the source units the entry names with PART, in PART source order. PART SOURCE is one PATH with one relative STRING, resolved from the entry's source unit exactly as a relative IMPORT SOURCE PATH resolves from its importing document. PART KIND is the part's role and is one member of project_part_kinds. The part declares SPECIFICATION KIND equal to its PART KIND; a part declaring any other KIND except kind.project uses error.project.part_kind at the part's SPECIFICATION KIND value. A document whose KIND is a project part kind is legal only as a part of the evaluation root's project; as the evaluation root, or as an IMPORT or EXTENSION source, it uses error.project.placement at its SPECIFICATION KIND value. Two PART declarations of one project, or a PART and an IMPORT or EXTENSION of that project, that resolve to the same source unit use error.project.part_duplicate at the later SOURCE value in project source order.
project_contract.requiredness: PART REQUIRED defaults to TRUE. A required part whose source cannot be obtained uses error.project.part_missing at its PART SOURCE value. A part declared REQUIRED FALSE whose source is absent, meaning that the host reports that no source exists at its resolved path, is omitted: it contributes no source unit, declaration or diagnostic, and the evaluation records the omission. Every other failure to obtain an optional part's source uses error.project.part_missing, and an obtained optional part is processed exactly as a required part. Omission never satisfies a reference: a REF that only an omitted part could resolve uses error.reference.unresolved.
project_contract.order: Project source order is the entry, then each part in PART source order, then every IMPORT and EXTENSION unit in import resolution order; within one source unit it is lexical order. Wherever a contract orders by source position across source units, including FAILURE selection, handler candidate ordering, check prerequisite tie-breaks and diagnostic stable_order, a project evaluation compares source units in project source order before byte offsets. File system enumeration order, file creation or modification time, file name collation, locale collation and host traversal order are never ordering inputs.
project_contract.namespace: The entry and its parts share one project namespace, as if their top-level declarations were written in one document in project source order. An unqualified REF in the entry or in any part resolves in that namespace, and no role restricts visibility. IDs, SPECIFICATION IDs included, are unique across the project: an ID declared in two project units uses error.id.duplicate at the later declaration in project source order, and no declaration replaces another. IMPORT and EXTENSION namespaces declared by the entry are owned in the whole project namespace, so no declaration of any part may occupy an import-owned first identifier segment. The project namespace is resolved only when it is complete: every required part is obtained, and every obtained unit has passed the localization, lexical and grammar_or_schema stages and the part, placement and version rules. Otherwise no REF of the project is resolved, and no error.id.duplicate or error.reference.unresolved is inferred from the incomplete namespace; the diagnostics that made it incomplete reject the project.
project_contract.versions: Every project unit declares LCL VERSION 0.3.0; a part declaring another LCL version uses error.version.unsupported. Every part declares the entry's exact SPECIFICATION VERSION; a different version uses error.version.mismatch at the part's SPECIFICATION VERSION value. IMPORT and EXTENSION keep their exact version rules.
project_contract.authority: Every project unit is local specification. A declaration without AUTHORITY takes its own unit's SPECIFICATION AUTHORITY, and no import ceiling applies to a project part. Imported and extension declarations keep their import ceiling.
project_contract.check_selection: For check selection, the entry and every obtained part together are the EXECUTE root source document. Imported checks remain unselected unless an explicit reference selects them.
project_contract.localization: Localization applies to each project unit separately under 02_LEXICAL/13: each unit selects its own locale, and units of one project may select different locales. A localization-stage error in any obtained unit rejects the project.
project_contract.admission: A project is admitted exactly when processing steps 1 through 9 complete for the whole project with no unhandled diagnostic: every required part is obtained, every obtained unit passes the localization, lexical, grammar_or_schema, resolution, static_or_expression and validation stages, including its kind's top-level block legality, and every rule of this contract holds. No effect of a project evaluation precedes admission. A defect in any obtained unit rejects the whole project; there is no partial or best-effort project execution.
project_contract.standalone: A document of kind.task, kind.library, kind.extension, kind.data or kind.test keeps its standalone meaning, and project rules apply only when the evaluation root is a kind.project entry. A document declaring LCL VERSION 0.1.0 or 0.2.0 is processed only under that version's rules.
